chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The Muslims are bound by their conditions, except for every condition that contradicts the Book of Allah (Exalted and Glorious), which is not valid."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of contractual terms in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a foundational legal maxim (*usul*) in Shia jurisprudence, affirming the autonomy of contractual stipulations while setting the Quran as the ultimate boundary for validity. It clarifies that while parties have freedom to agree on terms, any clause violating explicit divine injunctions is null and void, a principle widely cited in discussions of *shurut al-'aqd* (conditions of contract).
